title: Personal Checking: The Extended Overdraft Fee on a Prolonged Negative Balance
content:
## Rule

A Personal Checking account whose ledger balance remains below zero for long enough is charged one extended overdraft fee for that negative episode.

- **The episode.** A negative episode opens on the day the ledger balance first dropped below zero; that day is held on the account record as the date the balance went negative. The episode closes when the balance at the end of a day is back at zero or higher, which also clears that date.
- **When the fee falls due.** The fee comes due once the tier's trigger period, in calendar days, has run from the day the balance first went negative. Day 1 of the count is the day after that date, and the fee is due on any date on or after that date plus the trigger period, the boundary day included.
- **How it is booked.** The fee is booked as an extended overdraft fee entry dated exactly the day the balance went negative plus the trigger period.
- **Once per episode.** A negative episode never carries more than one extended overdraft fee.
- **No fee on a zero-priced tier.** Where the tier's extended overdraft fee is 0.00, nothing is booked.
- **Other limits.** The daily cap on overdraft item fees does not restrict this fee. If the balance was restored to zero or above ahead of the due date, the fee is not charged.

Each tier applies its own fee and trigger period; the date the balance went negative is read from the account record.

## Timeline (hypothetical dates and a hypothetical trigger of 5 days)

| Balance first negative | Date checked | Balance still negative? | Fee due? | Fee entry dated |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 May 2026 | 14 May 2026 (day 4) | yes | no | — |
| 10 May 2026 | 15 May 2026 (day 5) | yes | yes | 15 May 2026 |
| 10 May 2026 | 20 May 2026 | yes | yes, and only once | 15 May 2026 |
| 10 May 2026 | 15 May 2026 | no, back to zero at the close of 13 May | no | — |

## Questions answered by the rule

**Does a second extended overdraft fee arise if the balance stays negative for twice the trigger period?** No; the episode carries one such fee.

**Does a new episode start a new count?** Yes. Once the balance recovers to zero or above, the date is cleared, and a later drop below zero opens a fresh episode with its own count.
